subject: Assessing vendor replacement: cost, credits, and packaging questions
messages:
From: Elena Rivas <elena.rivas@nexahq.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@nexahq.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Assessing vendor replacement: cost, credits, and packaging questions

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo this week — the latency profile you showed is compelling. We have two internal asks before we can recommend any vendor switch to the ops and procurement committee:

1) A clear commercial comparison that maps our current blended run-rate to your proposed consumption and any seat/commit alternatives. Please show: list price, proposed matched rate, and one-time migration credit (if any).
2) Packaging and operational caveats: what items are considered add-ons (VPC/private deploy, advanced observability retention, KMS/HSM integrations) and how they are billed — one-time vs recurring.
3) A realistic migration effort estimate (hours by role) and the recommended rollback/fallback plan.

We have a consultant (copied) who will validate migration timelines. For commercial context, Nexa is on VendorX today: blended effective rate ~ $0.020/token (inference + embedding mix), 18-month remaining commitment with approximate annual spend of $1.2M.

Can you share a short packet with: line-item economics, an example migration credit structure (one-time vs recurring), and a list of technical prerequisites that would increase onboarding scope? PDF or spreadsheet is fine.

Elena
Elena Rivas
Head of ML Platform, NexaHealth
elena.rivas@nexahq.com

Kimberly / Connor — looped you for pricing + implementation ops input. External asked for a line-item packet and migration estimate. Key constraints: Nexa is under an 18-month remaining commitment with VendorX (~$1.2M/year, blended $0.020/token). They care about: matched unit economics, migration credits, and clarity on add-on billing (VPC/KMS/observability retention).

Please draft a one-page commercial match (two options: consumption-match vs 12-month reserved tier) and a separate migration-estimate worksheet (hours by role: infra eng, data infra, platform, CS). Attach the workbook and short note. Prefer conservative timelines: we should call out tech risks that add time (KMS integration, custom auth).

Timeline: want to get back to Elena by EOD Fri (tomorrow) PDT.

Thanks — Soojin
Soogin Lee

soojin_lee@redwood.ai
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Fwd: Assessing vendor replacement: cost, credits, and packaging questions

Thanks Soojin — attaching the workbook (Nexa_econ_workbook.xlsx) and a short summary PDF. High-level recommendation and numbers below. Feel free to edit before sending externally.

Executive summary (two options):

Option A — Consumption match (aggressive, fast close)
- Match Nexa's blended effective rate: $0.020/token for first 12 months (applies to inference + embedding mix provided).
- One-time migration credit: $90,000 applied as invoice credit in month 1.
- Includes 40 hours of onboarding engineering support (week-of go-live), additional hours billed at $250/hr.
- Add-ons: VPC private deployment + KMS integration: $12k one-time + $1,200/month for managed KMS key rotation/monitoring (optional). Observability retention beyond 30 days: billed at $0.03/GB-month.

Option B — 12-month Reserved Tier (predictable, deeper discount)
- 12-month committed spend: $1.05M (10% discount vs current run-rate).
- Effective blended rate ~ $0.0168/token.
- One-time migration credit: $120,000 (spread across first two invoices if needed).
- Includes up to 120 hours of onboarding (includes runbook creation, KV cache tuning, and one-week on-site/remote cadence).
- Add-ons: same as above but included in reserved tier for first 3 months.

Migration estimate (risk adjusted):
- Infra eng: 80–140 hrs (networking, VPC peering, firewall rules).
- Platform/ML eng: 60–110 hrs (model validation, KV cache tuning, inference integration).
- Data infra: 40–80 hrs (ingest hooks, embedding alignment).
- CS/PM: 30–50 hrs (comms, runbook, go-live).
- Typical calendar: 4–8 weeks from kickoff for Option A; 6–10 weeks for Option B (more runway for reserved, broader scope).

Risks that increase estimate:
- Customer-managed HSM/HSM attestation requirements (~+2–3 weeks).
- Custom auth/token flows and SSO mapping (+1–2 weeks).
- Large historical KV cache priming (depends on model sequence lengths).

Attachments included: Nexa_econ_workbook.xlsx (line-item math), SOC2-Checklist.pdf (security artifacts we can provide), and a one-page summary.

Notes on pricing rationale: we matched close to their blended rate in Option A but limited onboarding hours to keep one-time cost exposure manageable. Option B reduces unit economics and increases onboarding scope to reduce operational risk during go-live — good for customers with heavy integration.

If everyone signs off, I can convert to a PDF and we can send to Elena with a short cover note.

- Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Sr. Pricing Strategy, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Assessing vendor replacement: cost, credits, and packaging questions

Hi Elena — appreciate the additional context and the spend numbers. Attached is a short packet that includes: 1) a one-page commercial summary with two matching options, 2) an econ workbook with line-item math, and 3) our SOC2 and security checklist. Attachments: Nexa_Redwood_Match_Case.pdf, Nexa_econ_workbook.xlsx, SOC2-Checklist.pdf.

Short version (read-first):
- If Nexa wants a like-for-like move with minimal ops risk, Option B (12-month reserved) gives the best blended unit economics (~$0.0168/token) and comes with the biggest migration credit ($120k) and expanded onboarding (up to 120 hrs).
- If Nexa prefers lowest upfront friction and retains consumption flex, Option A matches the current blended ~$0.020/token for 12 months with a $90k migration credit and limited onboarding (40 hrs).

Operational notes / prerequisites that affect time/cost:
- KMS/HSM: customer-managed HSM adds ~2–3 weeks; if Nexa wants us to manage keys we include the first 3 months of managed rotation in Option B.
- Private VPC: one-time network setup (~40–60 hrs) if they require dedicated VPC peering and firewall changes.
- Observability retention longer than 30 days will be billed as an add-on unless we include it in a reserved-tier addendum.

Next steps I propose:
1) Tell us which option you prefer (A vs B) and whether KMS/HSM is required.
2) If you approve Option B, we’ll prepare a short SOW + 1-page commercial amendment and a proposed kickoff date.
3) We can schedule a 30-minute technical sync with Connor and our Solutions team next week to validate the migration assumptions (I'll share the workbook ahead of time).

Tom — if you or procurement want a spreadsheet-friendly view of the migration hours for your PM, the workbook has a tab with role-by-role hour estimates.

Happy to jump on a call tomorrow afternoon if that helps.

Best —
